ai.literal: Wealth makes those who are of no worth into people of worth; other than wealth, there is no other thing of value.
ai.translation: Except wealth, there is nothing else that can make those of no consequence into people of consequence.
ai.modern: மதிப்பில்லாதவர்களை மதிப்புடையவர்களாக மாற்றும் ஆற்றல் செல்வத்திற்கு மட்டுமே உண்டு; அச்செல்வத்தைத் தவிர வேறு சிறந்த பொருள் எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the social power of wealth by playing on the multiple meanings of the word 'poruḷ'. First, 'poruḷ' refers to wealth, which has the unique power to transform 'allavar' (those of no worth) into 'poruḷ' (people of consequence and respect). Finally, the poet concludes that other than wealth, there is no other 'poruḷ' (thing of real substance or utility) that can achieve this. The verse shows how material wealth instantly alters social perception and elevates a person's status.

ai.literal: Those who have nothing, everyone will despise; the wealthy, everyone will do honor.
ai.translation: Everyone despises those who have nothing, while everyone shows honor and respect to the wealthy.
ai.modern: பொருள் இல்லாதவர்களை எல்லாரும் இகழ்ந்து பேசுவார்கள்; செல்வம் உடையவர்களை எல்லாரும் மதித்துச் சிறப்பு செய்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights a stark social reality regarding how wealth dictates human relationships and societal respect. The author observes that those who lack material wealth (illārai) are universally looked down upon or despised (eḷḷuvar) by everyone. Conversely, those who possess wealth (celvarai) are universally honored and treated with high regard (ciṟappu ceyvar). By contrasting the verbs 'eḷḷuvar' (despise) and 'ceyvar ciṟappu' (will do honor), the verse emphasizes that wealth is a primary driver of social standing and influence.

ai.literal: The unfailing lamp called wealth will destroy darkness, having gone to the thought-of country.
ai.translation: The unfailing lamp called wealth dispels darkness, reaching even the distant lands one intends to conquer.
ai.modern: பொருள் என்று சொல்லப்படும் அணையாத விளக்கு, தான் நினைத்த தேசத்திற்குச் சென்று அங்குள்ள பகையாகிய இருளை ஒழிக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares wealth to an inextinguishable lamp (பொய்யா விளக்கம்). Just as a physical lamp dispels darkness, wealth dispels the darkness of poverty, hostility, and obstacles. This unique lamp is so powerful that its light can be carried to any foreign land or territory that one intends to reach (எண்ணிய தேயத்துச் சென்று), removing all difficulties there as well.

ai.literal: Virtue it will yield, pleasure also it will yield, knowing the proper means, without evil, acquired wealth.
ai.translation: Wealth that is acquired by knowing the proper means and without committing any evil will yield both virtue and pleasure.
ai.modern: நல்வழியை அறிந்து, தீமை இல்லாமல் சேர்க்கப்பட்ட செல்வம், அறத்தையும் தரும்; இன்பத்தையும் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the dual benefits of wealth that is acquired through righteous and proper means. When wealth is earned without causing harm or committing evil deeds (தீதின்றி), and by understanding the correct, ethical methods (திறனறிந்து), it becomes a source of true goodness. Such ethically earned wealth not only enables a person to perform virtuous deeds (அறன் ஈனும்) but also brings genuine happiness and pleasure (இன்பமும் ஈனும்) to their life. The poet emphasizes that the moral quality of how wealth is acquired directly determines its ultimate value and the joy it brings.

ai.literal: With grace and with love, that does not come, wealth's accumulation, do not embrace, let it roll away.
ai.translation: Do not accept the accumulation of wealth that does not come with grace and love; cast it away and let it perish.
ai.modern: அருளோடும் அன்போடும் வராத செல்வத்தின் சேர்க்கையை ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாமல், அது அழிந்துபோகுமாறு விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ethical boundaries of acquiring wealth. It states that any prosperity or accumulation of wealth (ஆக்கம்) that is not earned through compassionate means (அருள்) and loving ways (அன்பு) must be rejected. The term 'புல்லார்' instructs us not to embrace or accept such unethical gains. Instead, one should let it roll away and perish (புரள விடல்), as wealth obtained without moral values brings no true benefit.

and the wealth seized by defeating

ai.literal: Unclaimed wealth and, customs duty revenue and, his enemies defeating wealth and, are the king's wealth.
ai.translation: Unclaimed property that accrues to the state, customs duties, and the tribute captured from defeated enemies are all the rightful revenues of a king.
ai.modern: வாரிசு இல்லாததால் அரசுக்குச் சேரும் பொருளும், சுங்க வரியாக வரும் பொருளும், தன் பகைவரை வென்று பெறும் பொருளும் அரசனுக்குரிய செல்வங்கள் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three legitimate sources of revenue that fill a state's treasury. The first is 'uṟuporuḷ', which refers to ownerless or unclaimed wealth, such as escheats, that naturally falls to the state. The second is 'ulku poruḷ', which represents customs duties and tolls collected on trade. The third is 'teṟuporuḷ', which is the tribute or booty acquired by defeating hostile enemies. Together, these three form the ethical and legal basis of a king's wealth.

ai.literal: The infant called grace, yielded by love, is sustained by the precious foster-mother called wealth.
ai.translation: The child called compassion, born of love, is nurtured and sustained by the bountiful foster-mother called wealth.
ai.modern: அன்பு பெற்றெடுத்த அருள் என்னும் குழந்தையானது, பொருள் என்னும் வளமையான செவிலித்தாயால் வளர்க்கப்பட்டு உயிர்வாழும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful family metaphor to explain the practical necessity of wealth. Compassion (அருள்) is described as a child born to the mother called love (அன்பு). However, just as a newborn child needs a foster-mother (செவிலி) to feed and nurture it so it can grow, compassion cannot survive or be put into practice in the real world without the support of material wealth (பொருள்). Thus, wealth is essential to sustain and realize one's compassionate intentions.

words.gloss: with something of one's own in hand

ai.literal: Having climbed a hill, watching an elephant fight is like, one's own hand-wealth something having, he who performs action.
ai.translation: Undertaking a task with one's own wealth in hand is like watching an elephant fight from the safety of a hilltop.
ai.modern: தன் கையில் சொந்தப் பொருள் இருக்க ஒருவன் ஒரு செயலைச் செய்வது, குன்றின் மேல் ஏறி நின்று யானைச் சண்டையைக் காண்பது போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the security and confidence that comes from undertaking an enterprise with one's own capital. The poet compares this to watching an elephant fight from the safety of a hilltop ('kunṟēṟi'). Just as a spectator on a hill is completely safe from the dangers of the rampaging beasts below, a person who starts a task with their own secure funds ('taṉkaittoṉṟu uṇṭāka') is protected from the risks and anxieties of dependency. The vivid analogy emphasizes that self-reliance ensures both safety and success in any venture.

ai.literal: Make wealth; to cut the pride of enemies, a steel weapon sharper than that, there is nothing.
ai.translation: Accumulate wealth; there is no sharper steel than it to cut down the pride of your enemies.
ai.modern: பொருளைச் சம்பாதியுங்கள்; பகைவரின் செருக்கை அழிக்கும் கூர்மையான ஆயுதம் அதைவிட வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense practical power of acquiring wealth. The poet advises us to earn and accumulate wealth, describing it as the ultimate instrument of defense and influence. To cut down the arrogance and pride of one's enemies, there is no steel weapon sharper than the possession of wealth. When one is financially strong, adversaries naturally lose their power to oppose, making wealth more effective than any physical blade.

ai.literal: To those who have acquired excellent wealth abundantly, the other two are easy things together.
ai.translation: To those who have abundantly acquired glorious wealth, the other two values of life (virtue and pleasure) become easily attainable together.
ai.modern: சிறந்த செல்வத்தை மிகுதியாக ஈட்டியவர்களுக்கு, மற்ற இரு உறுதிகளாகிய அறமும் இன்பமும் எளிதாகக் கிடைக்கக்கூடிய பொருள்களாக ஒருசேர அமைந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme practical utility of wealth in achieving the other goals of life. 'ஒண்பொருள்' refers to glorious, rightfully earned wealth, and 'காழ்ப்ப' means to accumulate it in solid abundance. For those who possess such wealth, the other two aspects of human life—virtue (அறம்) and pleasure (இன்பம்)—become 'எண்பொருள்' (easy things) that can be attained together ('ஒருங்கு') without arduous effort. Wealth serves as the enabling instrument that naturally brings righteous deeds and worldly happiness within one's reach.
